text: Repairs: paint walls and touch up scuffs, caulk a tub or sink, patch small holes, sand, regrout, pressure-wash, seal a deck.
Pests: remove insects and spiders, clean ant trails, set and check traps, report droppings or nests, empty standing water, pantry-moth and fruit-fly traps.

Away mode. Your departure routine covers daily exits. Add a vacation or house-sitting mode: arm the alarm, set lights on timers, bring in mail and packages, water plants, check for leaks and pests, run taps, check the freezer after an outage, care for pets, send status photos.

Pets beyond feeding and walking. Give owner-directed medication, bathe and dry a dog, check for ticks and fleas, open and close crates, keep pets' meals separate, calm a pet during storms or fireworks. Aquarium water changes, filter, and glass, small-animal cages, and backyard chickens (eggs, coop, water) are also missing.

Technique: carve, fillet, shuck; awkward produce (squash, pineapple, mango, coconut); baking steps (grease and line pans, proof dough, cool on racks, frost); grilling (light, flip, check temperature, propane level); disposing of cooking oil; espresso with steamed milk, pour-over.

Vehicles, bikes, and errands (only if scope goes past the property line). Refuel, check and inflate tires, top off washer fluid, change wipers, jump-start, change a flat, scrape ice and snow, check the back seat before locking, check a car seat; lube a bike chain, patch a flat, charge an e-bike; curbside pickup, pharmacy, post office, donation and return drop-offs.
“Finish whatever I forgot to do.” It needs to inspect the environment and infer incomplete chores.
“Prepare everything I’ll need tomorrow.” Requires reasoning from calendar/context, weather, activities, school/work needs, and personal habits.
“Find something heavy enough to hold this down.” Requires approximate physics reasoning.
“Find something waterproof to put under this.” Requires material-property reasoning.
“Figure out why the floor is wet.” Could be spilled water, a leak, pet water, rain, appliance overflow, etc.
“Untangle the garden hose.” Larger-scale flexible-object planning.
“Move those chairs into the shade.” Shade changes spatially over time.
“Make this safe for the dog.” Requires pet-specific hazard reasoning.
“Watch me do this once, then do the others.” Few-shot physical learning.
“If it starts raining, close the windows.” Requires conditional rules that persist for days.
“Run the house while we’re away for a week.” Requires long-horizon autonomy, contingency handling, and knowing when to escalate.
“Get ready for the storm / the plumber / the newborn.” Requires building an event-specific prep list from context.
